solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Makes prisoner swagger around cold square

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: around tells us the swagger word is wrapped about the cold letter

parts.note: to swagger is to strut
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An inmate struts arrogantly round a chilly prison yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct something is to build or make it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Awfully verbose remark

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so verbose is mangled into new order

explanation.surface: A comment that is terribly long-winded.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to comment or remark, as in 'he observed that it was late'.

clue.text: Last of poseurs with muscles — you can see right through them

definitions.text: you can see right through them

indicators.note: Last of takes only the final letter of the word poseurs

parts.note: pecs are the pectoral chest muscles

explanation.surface: Musclebound show-offs are so transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see right through' sounds like seeing through a fake; it means looking through glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs, spectacles, are lenses you look through to see clearly.

clue.text: Catalogue in which you'll find student's present?

definitions.meaning: a catalogue is a list or record of items

definitions.text: in which you'll find student's present?
definitions.meaning: the class list read out at roll call records whether each pupil is present

explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official list; at school, the attendance list marks pupils present.

clue.text: Parts of logs — each is half-cut with strict care, draining energy

indicators.note: half-cut is British slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
draining says the energy letter is let out of the words strict care

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Bits of timber, each partly sawn with precise attention, lose their vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logs' suggests timber but means logarithms. 'draining' removes E from STRICT CARE; 'half-cut' rearranges EACH IS STRICTCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the characteristic is the whole-number part of a logarithm, alongside the mantissa.

clue.text: Steps by Conservatives finally could create a stir

indicators.note: could create says the words a stir can be made into something new by reordering
finally picks the last letter of Conservatives

explanation.surface: Tory moves could cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' here means beside, so the rearranged pair of words simply sits next to the final letter of the Tories; 'could create' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairs are a flight of steps between floors.

clue.text: Bachelor dropping off best son's food

indicators.note: dropping off says the bachelor letter falls away from the front of what follows

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A single man nods off over his best son's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAT plus S gives BEATS; taking B away, as 'dropping off' signals, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, as in a snack bar sign offering good eats.

clue.text: Found his belt's twisted round middle of chair

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters wrap about the central chair letter
twisted says the letters of his and belt's are contorted into another order
middle of takes the central letter of chair

explanation.surface: Someone discovered his belt was wrapped around a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' tempts as the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning to set up; the possessive 's of belt's supplies a letter to the twisted pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, establish it.

clue.text: Where you might find ham sandwich a treat initially in that place

indicators.note: sandwich as a verb means the outer word is split to hold the inner letters

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of treat

explanation.surface: Where one might find a ham sandwich as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the sandwich filling; it is a ham actor, found on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a showy, overacting performer, someone found in a playhouse.

clue.text: Abandoned, Crusoe finally is left here?

definitions.text: Abandoned, Crusoe finally is left here?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests letters cast about wildly, so the pieces that follow are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the castaway's name

explanation.surface: A castaway wonders whether this is the place he was finally marooned.
explanation.walkthrough: E (end of Crusoe), IS and L are rearranged as 'Abandoned' signals; the whole clue also describes where Robinson Crusoe was left.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe was marooned on a small island, which a poetic word for island names.

clue.text: Stands behind guest near a stranger

indicators.note: stranger read as more strange tells us the preceding letters come out oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind a visitor who is close to an unknown person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person but works as 'more strange', the anagram signal for GUEST NEAR A.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand behind a promise or product is to guarantee it, back it up.

clue.text: Biting small snack

parts.note: biting air or wit can be called crisp, sharp and fresh
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A small snack that crunches when bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain crisps are thin fried potato slices, what Americans call chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisps are a packaged savoury nibble, an everyday light bite in Britain.

clue.text: A bar annoyed with cost for tumblers

indicators.note: annoyed, as if ruffled and stirred up, signals that the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub owner is irritated by the price of drinking glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumblers' suggests glasses in a bar, but here it means people who tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers are performers doing somersaults and flips, the same as circus gymnasts.

clue.text: Flimsy stupidly tries, without resistance, to get most tipsy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the resistance letter beside, not within, the rearranged letters

parts.note: Flimsy is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to themself as me
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: stupidly says the word tries is muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: The setter foolishly attempts, with no opposition, to get very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: ME (Flimsy the setter) is followed by R set outside RIEST, the rearrangement of TRIES signalled by 'stupidly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a mild word for drunk, so the superlative means the most tipsy.

clue.text: I can store up responses

indicators.note: up in the sense of stirred up says the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they can stockpile replies.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactions are responses to a stimulus or event.

clue.text: Some cut-price shows — they may be held in the summer

definitions.text: they may be held in the summer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bargain entertainments, the sort staged in summertime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' suggests shows being staged; it is ice creams held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices are ice creams or sorbets, held in the hand on hot summer days.

clue.text: Privation's severe on boat

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, so the definition is privation itself

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first word on top of the second

parts.note: hard means severe, as in a hard winter
a ship is a large boat

explanation.surface: Lack of necessities is harsh aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship and privation both mean suffering from lack of necessities.

clue.text: Vast area of land where silicon's found in volcanic rock

indicators.note: found in says the silicon symbol sits inside the rock word

parts.note: aa is a rough, clinkery kind of solidified lava
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: A geological description of where silicon occurs in volcanic stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a huge landmass.

clue.text: Starts dressing, we hear, with son

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is said aloud and a similar-sounding one written

parts.note: a sauce is a dressing for food

explanation.surface: Begins getting dressed, apparently, alongside a son.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Sources are origins or starting points, as a river's source is where it starts.

clue.text: Communicating with pastor, leaving what he should be doing?

indicators.note: leaving says the pastor's letter departs from the longer word

parts.note: a pastor ought to be giving sermons, that is preaching

explanation.surface: A churchgoer complains that the pastor is chatting instead of giving his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue word 'pastor' does two things in the surface but gives only P in the wordplay; 'he' refers back to him.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone is to get through to them, to contact or communicate with them.

clue.text: Disgusting sound — old male's implicated

indicators.note: implicated, folded in, says the old male letters are wrapped inside the sound word

parts.note: a noise is a sound
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A revolting noise, and an elderly man is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Noisome has nothing to do with noise: it means offensive, though its spelling tempts that link.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or foul-smelling, so revolting.

clue.text: Fruit boy stuck on nail

indicators.note: stuck on in a down clue places the boy above, attached to, the nail word

parts.note: Pip is a boy's name, the young hero of Great Expectations
a pin is a small nail

explanation.surface: A lad has impaled an apple on a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pippin is a variety of eating apple, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Caught us catching train frantically — they're often shut at night

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: catching tells us the us letters hold the rearranged train inside them
frantically says the letters of train are jumbled

explanation.surface: Passengers say they were seized while desperately catching a train late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching train' reads as boarding a train, but 'catching' is the container signal and 'frantically' the anagram one; C for caught is a cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains are drapes drawn closed over windows in the evening.

clue.text: Cut end off document?

definitions.meaning: to ... is, taken literally, to remove the tail end
to document something is to set it out item by item, describe it fully

explanation.definitionFit: Detailing a matter means recording it fully, so it can mean document; read as de-tail it means remove the end.

clue.text: Mammal one caught in trap, wickedly

indicators.note: caught in says the one letter is held inside the rearranged trap letters
wickedly signals the letters of trap are twisted around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal is cruelly snared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' puts I inside TAPR, the rearrangement of TRAP from 'wickedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal with a short trunk, found in South America and Asia.

clue.text: MP with colic has reforms to carry out

indicators.note: reforms read as re-forms says the letters are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A politician suffering stomach pains has changes to push through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a politician's policy noun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish a task is to carry it out, complete it successfully.

clue.text: Secret scheme to get lecturer into cannabis

indicators.note: into says the lecturer letter is placed inside the cannabis word

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A covert plan to get an academic involved with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a conspiracy, a secret plan.

clue.text: Exercises with energy on board american ship

indicators.note: on board says the energy letter is aboard, inside, the ship abbreviation

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, prefixes US naval vessels
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Sailors exercise energetically aboard a US Navy vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to use it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: A pryer knows when wife's rejected — exciting gossip

indicators.note: exciting, stirring up, signals that the letters are rearranged
rejected says the wife's letter is thrown out of the word knows

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A snoop learns of a wife being spurned, which makes for thrilling tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns KNOWS into KNOS; 'exciting' then rearranges A PRYER KNOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy parker is a busybody, someone who meddles in others' affairs; gossip can name such a person.
